name: Riesenrundgemälde
kurzbeschreibung: The Giant Cyclorama at the Tirol Panorama on Bergisel presents the dramatic 1809 Battles of Bergisel across 1,000 square metres of canvas in a 360-degree spectacle.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Innsbruck Giant Cyclorama (Riesenrundgemälde) housed inside the modern Tirol Panorama museum on historic Bergisel hill is a monumental masterpiece of European historical painting. As one of the world's few surviving 19th-century panoramic paintings, it spans a breathtaking 1,000 square metres of seamless circular canvas. Created in 1896 by Michael Zeno Diemer and his fellow artists, the panoramic painting immortalises the third Battle of Bergisel fought on August 13, 1809. Standing on the viewing rotunda, guests are immersed in the raw drama of Andreas Hofer's Tyrolean freedom uprising, framed by the authentic topography of the Inn Valley and the rugged peaks of the Nordkette.

Route & Requirements

The museum at Bergisel is designed to modern accessibility standards, ensuring comfortable visits for guests of all ages. The viewing platform circling the cyclorama and the subterranean permanent exhibition 'Schauplatz Tirol' are completely step-free, served by spacious elevators and gentle ramps. Visitors should allocate approximately one and a half to two hours to experience the cyclorama and the accompanying multimedia historical displays. Because the entire exhibition is indoors, it serves as a splendid all-weather cultural destination for independent travellers and families with prams.

Visiting & Getting There

The Tirol Panorama is located on Bergisel south of Innsbruck city centre. Tram line 1 or the historic Stubaitalbahn (STB) to the Bergisel stop, alongside the Sightseer tourist bus, connect the museum to Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof in just minutes. Paid parking facilities are available directly on the Bergisel plateau for motorists. The museum is open year-round from Wednesday to Monday (closed Tuesdays). Combined museum tickets offer discounted admission to other Tyrolean state museum sites including the Ferdinandeum.

Tips

A masterstroke of lighting and sculpted three-dimensional foreground (faux terrain) blurs the boundary between painted canvas and real terrain in stunning fashion. After exploring the museum, stroll along the scenic Bergisel circular path for sweeping vistas over the turbulent Sill Gorge and Innsbruck's historic roofs. Do not miss visiting the neighbouring Bergisel Ski Jump, designed by world-renowned architect Zaha Hadid, featuring a tower restaurant with sweeping alpine panoramas.
